subject: Comparing constrained model and general model using measurement invariance analyses

messages.author: 6db3c86d422c5ae9
messages.subject: Comparing constrained model and general model using measurement invariance analyses
parts:
Hello lavaan group,

I am conducting a cross-lagged panel model using lavaan. My general model is acceptable fit. Now I want to test if the model is the same across gender (constrained model). I was suggested to test the difference in chi-square between the general model and the constrained model. But I am still wondering whether I should test the model of configural using measurement invariance analysis, in which the group is "Gender". The model is as following:
modelconfig <- cfa(mymodel, data = mydata, group = 'Gender', estimator = 'MLR', missing = 'FIML') 
So can anyone show me if the modelconfig is suitable to test if the general model is the same across gender?

Another question I would like to consult you is that when I use command measurementInvariance(mymodel, data = mydata, group = 'Gender', estimator = 'MLR', missing = 'FIML'), I am always receiving a warning message as following: Error in if (cd < 0) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
But when I used the command to test configural model, the warning message disappeared. I can not solve the problem. Thus, can anyone please help me to solve it?

Thank you very much for considering my request,

Best,

Torres

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Comparing constrained model and general model using measurement invariance analyses
parts: I want to test if the model is the same across gender (constrained model). I was suggested to test the difference in chi-square between the general model and the constrained model. But I am still wondering whether I should test the model of configural using measurement invariance analysis, in which the group is "Gender".

The test of model fit is not specifically a test of whether that model fits equally across groups.  See this article about using a permutation test of configural invariance:

http://dx.doi.org/10.1037/met0000152

The permutation test is automated for lavaan models in the semTools package.  See the ?permuteMeasEq help page.
Error in if (cd < 0) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

This looks like the scaling factor might be missing.  When you fit the model yourself (without the measurementInvariance() function), did you notice missing values in the Robust column of the summary() output?
But when I used the command to test configural model, the warning message disappeared.

When you used which command?  Just the cfa() function?

If the scaling factor cannot be computed for some reason, then you won't be able to calculate robust test statistics to compare models.  But permutation tests could be a solution, because they do not require the robust test statistic to have nominal Type I error rates:

https://doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2017.1421467

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.author: d16c9a3215b10e4b
messages.subject: Re: Comparing constrained model and general model using measurement invariance analyses
parts:
Dear all

I have a related question regarding the application of permuteMeasEq for SB scaled chi-square statistics in MGCFA estimated by ULSM.

As ULSM is my estimator, the original chi-square statistics were incorrect and for nest model comparisons, the difference in chi-square statistics needed to be robustified.

My question is: when I use permuteMeasEq to evaluate the difference in chi-square statistics in MGCFA, which version of the difference in chi-square statistics should I target?

For the results of measurementInvariance, only "chisq" and "chisq.scaled" are available and there is no robustified "chisq" for permutation tests.

I am not sure if permutation tests of "chisq" or "chisq.scaled" is a reasonable method to evaluate measurement invariance as that for AFIs (e.g. robust CFI, robust RMSEA)?

The R codes in the supplementary materials provided by Terrence ( http://dx.doi.org/10.1037/met0000152.supp ) use both "chisq" and "chisq.scaled" as targets of permutation tests.
Since I did not have the full-text of that paper, I have no idea how this issue was dealt with by the authors.

Thanks a lot!

Best,
KC

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Comparing constrained model and general model using measurement invariance analyses
parts: My question is: when I use permuteMeasEq to evaluate the difference in chi-square statistics in MGCFA, which version of the difference in chi-square statistics should I target?

The whole point of the permutation test is that it doesn't matter.  In this paper with categorical data, we permuted the naïve chi-squared statistic, which resulted in more nominal Type I error rates than the analytical robust chi-squared

https://doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2017.1421467

I am not sure if permutation tests of "chisq" or "chisq.scaled" is a reasonable method to evaluate measurement invariance as that for AFIs (e.g. robust CFI, robust RMSEA)?

The R codes in the supplementary materials provided by Terrence ( http://dx.doi.org/10.1037/met0000152.supp ) use both "chisq" and "chisq.scaled" as targets of permutation tests.
Since I did not have the full-text of that paper, I have no idea how this issue was dealt with by the authors.

Results showed that permutation of both naïve and robust chi-squared statistics, as well as any fit index, provides the same results (with only minor deviations due to sampling error).  So within a particular sample, the p values might not all match across different fit measures, but they all have nominal error rates if the exchangeability assumption is met (i.e., groups have distributions with similar shapes, not necessarily normal).  
 
I attached the accepted version of the paper (preprint).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
